data.content_ref: inline:The isolated artifact ABSTRACTS from SRC_003's concrete content-addressable and sequence-numbered append mechanisms to a general principle: safety of an append-only log is a property of replay semantics, not of the write primitive. The specific deduplication strategy (content hash, producer+sequence, UUID) is an implementation detail; the abstract principle is that replay must produce the same reasoning state regardless of duplicate physical entries. This abstraction explains why all three of SRC_001's archetypes (random UUID, deterministic hash, global counter) can be evaluated on a single axis: does the replay engine's deduplication logic, combined with the writer's keying strategy, yield a deterministic post-replay state? REFUTED IF the isolated artifact's abstraction turns out to be too coarse—i.e., if different deduplication strategies produce materially different correctness properties under partial failure or concurrent writes, so that 'safety is a replay property' conceals real distinctions between content-hash deduplication and sequence-number deduplication that matter for system correctness.
